items_missed: Never asked "How are you today?" as a warmth/rapport check at the open
No explicit agenda statement ("I'll gather details, then walk you through pricing, takes about 10-15 minutes") or an explicit "sound good?" confirmation
Did not ask whether the customer needed packing services
Did not ask the moving-stressors question ("is there anything you're particularly worried about with this move?")
Never confirmed zip codes for the origin (Public Storage) or destination (apartment) addresses
No Worries Damage Coverage ($2,000 accidental damage protection) never mentioned
Meet Your Mover program (mover photo/bio email before the move) never mentioned
On-Time Guarantee (discounting if the arrival window is missed) never mentioned, despite a long discussion about POD delivery timing uncertainty where it would have landed well
No concrete equivalents/comparisons used to make the time estimate tangible (e.g., school-bus-load reference)

Entire Save Your Ass prep speech skipped — no consolidation tips (boxes, loose drawer items), no "take a carload" tip, no sense-check close for that topic, despite a ~100-125 box move that would benefit most from it

Did not attempt to lock in a booking on the call itself (understandable given the POD delivery date is still unconfirmed, but no explicit "want to go ahead and get this on the schedule" attempt was made)
No mention of a bolded detail-confirmation list at the top of the estimate email or a "reply with any corrections" verification step
No insurance explanation (No Worries coverage + 60 cents/lb baseline liability) given, even though a safe and other furniture were flagged as move contents
No genuine rapport/humor moment — call stayed warm but strictly transactional throughout
top_strength: Grant handled a genuinely unusual, multi-part move (two PODs splitting between a storage unit and a second-floor apartment) with patient, methodical discovery — nailing down box counts, the safe's weight limit, and access details — and proactively walked the customer through the realistic uncertainty of POD delivery timing without her having to push for it.
coaching_note: The single highest-leverage fix is that the Save Your Ass prep speech was skipped entirely (0/10) — on a ~100-125 box move split across two destinations, walking Jenny through consolidation tips and the "take a carload" trick could materially cut billable hours, and Grant should build it in as a standard close to every pricing conversation, not just an afterthought.
phone_presence_notes: Grant used consistent, natural warmth ("no problem," "of course," "for sure, for sure") and the customer's name throughout, keeping her comfortable and engaged through a genuinely complicated move.
